info.title: Dispatch API
info.description:
Dispatch is a self-hosted email API on Amazon SES with a Resend-shaped interface. Routes have no version prefix.

Authentication: send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` with an API key or a `sess_` session token. Routes marked `x-scope: send` accept a sending-access key. Every other authenticated route needs a full-access key. A session takes its access from the user's role: `full` calls every route, and `read` without `full` (the Viewer role) calls `GET` routes, `POST /me/password`, and `DELETE /sessions/{id}` for its own sessions. Anything else gets `forbidden`. A viewer never sees a webhook signing secret, and log bodies shown to a viewer have share links and signed file URLs replaced with `[redacted]`. Public routes have `security: []`.

Shapes: a single resource is a flat object with `object` naming its type. A list is `{ object: "list", has_more, data }` and pages with `limit` (1 to 100, default 20), `after`, and `before`, which are item IDs and cannot be combined. A delete returns `{ object, id, deleted: true }`. Every JSON object response carries `request_id`.

Errors: `{ name, statusCode, message, request_id }`. Body validation failures are `validation_error` with status 400. A unique-value race is `validation_error` with status 409.

Rate limits: requests made with an API key share one bucket per tenant per second (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND`, default 10). A dashboard session has its own bucket per user (`SESSION_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND`, default 40). Public routes are limited per client IP and route (`PUBLIC_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND`, default 50, and `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND`, default 5, for `POST /sessions`). Responses to authenticated requests carry `ratelimit-limit`, `ratelimit-remaining`, and `ratelimit-reset`. A 429 adds `retry-after`.

post.description: Full access only. Locks latest versions and skips edited/custom copies. Existing sending settings and variable names are retained. Does not install missing templates or publish draft copies.

The email is stored before the response. With topic_id, Marketing sends carry protected unsubscribe headers and recipient-specific links. Multiple To, Cc, and Bcc recipients are deduplicated case-insensitively, first role wins, and split into separate To-only emails. The response retains the first id and adds emails: [{id, to, sandbox}]. Opted-out recipients fail independently. Idempotency covers the whole request. Transactional sends without topic_id keep their multi-recipient shape. Recipients at example.com, example.net, example.org and their subdomains, under .test, .example or .invalid, or at tenant sandbox_domains and their subdomains never reach the provider, even in production. Only real recipients in mixed emails are sent. sandbox describes the email identified by id; it is true only when all its original recipients are sandbox recipients. A sending-access key restricted to a domain can only send from that domain (`validation_error`, 403). An unverified sender domain fails with `validation_error` and status 403.

get.description: Counts real `email_events` for the tenant. Simulated email and sandbox-recipient activity is excluded from totals and rates, including automation and step breakdowns. Event attribution preserves historical real metrics when a later retry becomes sandbox. Without dates it covers the 7 days before now. `end_date` is exclusive. Rates are percentages rounded to two decimals, and 0 when the denominator is 0. `unsubscribed` counts `email.unsubscribed` events from Marketing and broadcast links. Automation attribution is worker-owned; legacy messages can have a null step key.

post.description: Stores the event and returns 202. The runs it starts, and the waiting runs it resumes, are stored with it, and the worker executes them afterward. When `email` matches no contact, the route adds one first: lowercased, subscribed, named from the payload's `first_name` and `last_name` (strings of 1 to 120 characters after trimming), and announced with `contact.created`. A live contact with no name gets the event's name, announced with `contact.updated`. A deleted contact is not brought back. Its runs start, and steps that change the contact, add it to a segment, or send it subscription mail skip it. A payload that breaks the event's schema fails with `validation_error` (422), and an unknown `contact_id` with `not_found` (404).

post.summary: Sign in with an email and password
post.description:
Trades a user's email and password for a `sess_` token that lasts 30 days. A wrong password, an unknown email, a deactivated user, and a user with no membership all get the same 401 `invalid_credentials`. After 10 failures for one email within 15 minutes, every attempt for that email gets 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` until the window ends. Also rate limited per client IP by `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND`.

For local development and tests, `api_key` in place of `password` exchanges a full-access key instead. That fails with `forbidden` unless `ALLOW_PASSWORDLESS_SESSIONS` is `true`, the default outside production.

Rule.description: Shared contact/event grammar. Segment context excludes event fields, limits five total levels/twenty conditions and permits email.sent/delivered/opened/clicked/bounced boolean eq/neq with optional exclusive automation_id/broadcast_id scope and positive duration window. Email facts mean existence, exclude sandbox and use the inclusive recorded-event interval [statement time-duration, statement time]. No window means all recorded time; negative facts also match never-sent contacts. Automation contexts explicitly refuse email engagement. contact.segments in segments references static membership only; automation context includes fresh matched dynamic IDs. Legacy own properties retain precedence. event.received_at is immutable. within/not_within take positive durations; invalid dates match neither. SQL supports finite numeric and ISO values with malformed legacy guards, not universal JavaScript legacy-parser equivalence.

window.description: Email engagement only: positive finite shared duration, such as 30 days.

SendEmailConfig.description: Automation Send email config. Transactional has no topic and does not enforce Marketing opt-outs. Marketing respects opt-outs and adds recipient-specific unsubscribe links and one-click headers. Omitted kind is accepted for legacy input and inferred as marketing when topic_id is present, otherwise transactional. Stored configs and responses always include kind. Disabled or paused drafts may keep Marketing steps without a topic, but create enabled, enable, or resume returns 422 until every Marketing step has a live topic. A Marketing template cannot be used transactionally. Runtime refuses a Marketing send if its topic is missing or deleted; it never falls back to Transactional.

kind.description: Optional for legacy input only. Marketing drafts may omit topic_id; Transactional cannot have topic_id.

topic_id.description: Allowed only for Marketing. A live topic is required before enabling or resuming, but may be omitted in a disabled or paused draft.

variable_mapping.description: Maps template variable names to dotted event.* or contact.* fields. Mappings override literal variables, read own properties only, and omit missing values. Fresh recipient and unsubscribe context stays protected.

StoredSendEmailConfig.description: Normalized automation Send email config. Responses always include the explicit kind, including for legacy input and incomplete Marketing drafts.

TriggerConfig.description: Contact triggers use their internal namespace and never wake event waits. Legacy {event_name} inputs normalize to type:event. New event and wait names cannot start with @; old stored event names remain unchanged in responses.

event_name.description: New input names cannot start with @. Legacy stored event names are preserved in responses.

field.description: Built-in or declared contact field, without contact. A field is required when from or to is supplied.

ExitConfig.description: An empty config. Exit ends the run deliberately with exit_reason exit and has no outgoing connections.

FilterConfig.description: next evaluates the rule once. following also saves a guard on the run, evaluated against fresh contact context and the run's triggering event before every later step, including Delay and Wait for event steps and resumed waits. Every saved guard must match. A failed Filter or guard ends the run with exit_reason filter and never follows a default connection. Already queued emails are not cancelled.

BranchConfig.description: Two to ten ordered paths with unique keys, validated by the API. Keys are nonempty and otherwise is reserved. Rules use fresh contact context and the run's triggering event. First-match routing evaluates paths in array order and takes the first matching rule; otherwise is implicit and chosen only when no rule matches. Each configured path and otherwise needs exactly one keyed branch connection. The step output records { path }.

SplitConfig.description: 2–4 unique stable keys. Whole-number weights sum to100; zero is allowed. Each variant, including zero-weight variants, needs exactly one variant edge with path=key. Assignment hashes only UTF8 run_id with SHA256, unsigned big-endian first4 bytes modulo100, against cumulative weights in order. Recorded {variant:key} survives retries and weight edits.

config.description: Config depends on type: send_email uses SendEmailConfig, condition uses Rule, filter uses FilterConfig, branch uses BranchConfig, split uses SplitConfig, exit uses empty ExitConfig. Marketing requires a live topic before enable/resume and cannot fall back to Transactional. Variables retain literal data. Splits record a stable variant and route via variant edges.

path.description: Required for branch (configured path or otherwise) and variant (configured variant key). Other types cannot carry path.

AutomationConnection.description: Branch connections start only at Branch steps; every configured path and otherwise requires exactly one keyed edge. Variant connections start only at Split steps; every configured variant, including weight0, requires exactly one edge with path=key. Every target must be a real step, including Exit. Exit has no outgoing connections. Filter steps have only a default connection, never followed on failure.

trigger.description: Event name. Used by the linear form. Contact triggers use a keyed trigger step with TriggerConfig.

reentry.description: Defaults to once for new contact triggers and every_time for event triggers.

steps.description: Graph form: keyed steps (`AutomationStep`) with `connections`. Linear form: unkeyed steps run in order after `trigger`.

AutomationInput.description: Branch steps require exactly one outgoing branch connection per configured path key and one for otherwise. Split steps require exactly one variant connection per unique configured key, including zero-weight variants. Only branch/variant connections carry path. Each target is a real step; Exit has no outgoing connections. Filters can use only a default connection and never follow it on failure. The API validates unique step/path keys, connection sources and targets, and an acyclic graph. Disabled Marketing drafts may omit a send step's topic_id. Creating enabled returns 422 until each Marketing step has a live topic. Send configs normalize legacy omitted kind from topic_id, and Marketing templates cannot be used transactionally.

expected_version.description: Optional optimistic guard; stale versions return409 without writes.

reentry.description: Changing trigger type retains the stored reentry value.

AutomationUpdate.description: Changing steps, connections, or trigger requires an already paused or disabled automation, or disabling in the same request. Previously used keys cannot change type. Branch steps require exactly one outgoing branch connection per configured path key and one for otherwise. Split steps require exactly one variant connection per unique configured key, including zero-weight variants. Only branch/variant connections carry path. Each target is a real step; Exit has no outgoing connections. Filters can use only a default connection and never follow it on failure. The API validates unique step/path keys, connection sources and targets, and an acyclic graph. Disabled or paused Marketing drafts may omit a send step's topic_id. Enabling or resuming returns 422 until each Marketing step has a live topic. Marketing templates cannot be used transactionally.

exit_reason.description: completed is a natural ending; exit is an Exit step; filter is a failed Filter or saved guard; stopped is cancellation; stranded is a paused edit that removed or changed the next step. Running and failed runs have null; failed is not an exit reason.

guards.description: Saved following-filter guards, empty when no following filter was saved. Checked against fresh context before every later step, including resumed waits.

AutomationRun.description: Exit reasons explain normal completion or cancellation without changing run statuses. Failed runs carry null exit_reason and their failure in error.

request_body.description: Redacted request body, or null. Secrets show as `[redacted]`.

ready.description: True when a tenant exists. For an anonymous caller this is the only field with a value.

api_key.description: Local development only, in place of `password`: a full-access API key for the same tenant. Refused unless `ALLOW_PASSWORDLESS_SESSIONS` is `true`.

SessionInput.description: Send `password`, or `api_key` for local development. Not both.

token.description: A `sess_` bearer token. Shown only once.

scope.description: What the caller may do. `read` is a dashboard session whose role can only read.

password.description: The user's first password. Without one, the user cannot sign in until an admin sets one with `PATCH /users/{id}`.

UserInput.description: An existing email is updated and reactivated.

password.description: A new password, which is how an admin resets a forgotten one. Ends the user's other sessions.

permissions.description: Defaults to `["full"]`. `full` grants every route. `read` without `full` grants `GET` routes, `POST /me/password`, and `DELETE /sessions/{id}` for the user's own sessions. Any other set grants nothing.

RoleInput.description: An existing name is updated and restored.

MembershipInput.description: A user has one membership. Posting again changes the role.

role.description: Role name. Present in list results.

sending.description: SES sending quota. Fixed sample values with the fake provider. Null when the lookup fails.

value.description: Counter value as a decimal string.

start.description: Inclusive start of the UTC calendar month.

end.description: Exclusive end of the UTC calendar month.

ses_estimate_usd.description: SES recipient destinations multiplied by the rate per 1,000; excludes other providers and is not rounded to cents.

days.description: Every UTC day in the selected month, including zero-filled days without activity.

templates.description: Referenced library slugs, not tenant template IDs.

AutomationPreset.description: Built-in graph with library-slug template references. Newsletter topic_id remains {{topic_id}} until installation. Event schemas type-check present fields, not required values; callers remain responsible for the actual runtime payload. No tenant resources are created by listing or reading a preset.

name.description: Defaults to the preset name; live name conflicts return 409.

from.description: Sender address, optionally Name <email>. Requires a live verified tenant domain with sending enabled.

topic_id.description: Live same-tenant topic, required for newsletter-welcome. Other Marketing presets may install disabled without it.

AutomationInstallation.description: Atomic disabled installation. Existing templates and compatible dependencies are reused unchanged; reused drafts are not published. Review before enabling.
